brief.headline: Memory supercycle tops as SK Hynix crashes -15%, HBM4 ramp fears hit Samsung; CoWoS still tight through Q4
brief.summary: <cite index="43-17,43-19">SK Hynix plunged 15% in Asia after KIS cut Q2 profit 8% below consensus on slower HBM4 shipments</cite>, dragging Samsung down 7-9% and <cite index="40-2,46-11">erasing $1.5 trillion across semis in under two weeks</cite>. <cite index="11-1,16-2,16-7">DRAM contract prices still climbing 58-63% QoQ in Q2 2026, NAND up 70-75%</cite>, but <cite index="13-26,13-27">spot buyers no longer chasing quotes—parabolic phase maturing</cite>. <cite index="21-6,26-2">Hyperscalers hit $725B capex in 2026, up 77% YoY</cite>, yet <cite index="29-3,29-4">Sequoia's $600B revenue gap widens as capex accelerates faster than AI monetization</cite>. <cite index="31-10">TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap narrows from 20% to 10% by end-2026</cite>, though <cite index="33-5">demand still exceeds supply</cite>.
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="4-11,4-17">SK Hynix holds 62% HBM shipment share (Q2 2025) and Goldman/UBS project 70% HBM4 share for Nvidia Rubin in 2026</cite>, sustaining the revenue-mix edge. <cite index="8-7,8-10">Samsung began HBM4 mass production in February 2026 and expects HBM sales to triple YoY</cite>, but <cite index="43-17">today's guide-down signals HBM4 qual/ramp risk persists</cite>. <cite index="2-20,2-21">Samsung passed Nvidia SiP tests; SK already supplying paid HBM4 samples</cite>—time-to-qual still favors SK. <cite index="5-9,5-10">SK shipped 12-layer HBM4E samples in June on schedule</cite> vs Samsung targeting HBM4E sampling H2. Near-term relative: long SK vs Samsung on product-cycle lead and margin trajectory, but watch for Samsung catch-up in H2 if 16-layer roadmap accelerates.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="13-10,18-4">Q1 DRAM surged 93-98% QoQ (record), Q2 moderates to 58-63%</cite>; <cite index="16-8">NAND accelerated from ~60% in Q1 to 70-75% in Q2</cite>. <cite index="14-22,21-6">Hyperscaler capex $725B drives server/HBM demand</cite>, but <cite index="11-4,11-5">consumer pricing pressure and smartphone caution emerging</cite>. <cite index="4-21,14-25">HBM capacity shift tightens general DRAM (3:1 wafer ratio)</cite>; <cite index="19-7">new fab capacity unlikely until late 2027/2028</cite>. First behavioral cracks: <cite index="13-26">buyers not chasing spot, NAND trading quiet</cite>. Cycle remains elevated but momentum peaked.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="4-7,4-9">HBM3E remains flagship in 2026, ~66% of total HBM shipments; HBM4 ramps gradually</cite>. <cite index="7-4,7-5">HBM3E pricing up ~20% for 2026 on H200 China approval (6 stacks each) and hyperscaler ASIC demand</cite>. <cite index="2-10,2-11">Nvidia exploring 16-layer HBM delivery Q4 2026</cite>, pulling forward generational shift before 12-layer HBM4 fully rolls out. <cite index="2-7,2-15">Rubin launch H2 2026 (8× HBM4 stacks) is the inflection</cite>. <cite index="5-11">SK's 12-layer HBM4E: 16 Gbps, >20% power improvement</cite>; <cite index="8-3,8-4">Samsung HBM4: 2,048 I/O, 40% power efficiency gain, 10% thermal resistance, 30% heat dissipation vs HBM3E</cite>. <cite index="6-14,6-16">TSMC C-HBM4E shifts to N3P (0.75V), base die to N12 (0.8V) for 1.5–2× efficiency</cite>. <cite index="7-12,7-13">2026 HBM mix forecast: 55% HBM4, 45% HBM3E, with HBM4 absorbing HBM3E demand from Q3</cite>.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix -15% on KIS downgrade; Q2 profit 8% below consensus on HBM4 shipment delays
news_pulse.implication: First material sell-side negative on HBM4 ramp timing. Tests bull thesis that assumed smooth dual-generation (HBM3E/HBM4) supply through 2026. Ripples across MU, WDC, Samsung.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung Q2 profit +1,810% YoY but shares -8%; record $59B op profit fails to impress
news_pulse.implication: Peak-earnings sell-off dynamic. Market pricing in memory-price deceleration and HBM qual risk despite record absolute numbers. Confirms cyclical top fears.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 capex revised to $725B, up from $365B estimate one year ago—BNP Paribas
news_pulse.implication: Capex nearly doubled in 12 months. Sustains HBM/server DRAM demand but widens Sequoia's $600B AI revenue gap, raising ROI scrutiny and capex-fatigue risk into H2.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap narrows 20%→10% by end-2026; capacity 115-140k wpm
news_pulse.implication: Easing but still tight. Nvidia locked 70%+ of CoWoS-L for 2025; 2026-27 bookings extend. Packaging remains gating factor for Blackwell/Rubin ramp, favoring early HBM suppliers.

news_pulse.headline: Nvidia asks suppliers for 16-layer HBM delivery Q4 2026; performance eval starts Q3
news_pulse.implication: Accelerates HBM4E roadmap ahead of 12-layer maturity. Raises technical bar (hybrid bonding, yield) and compresses Samsung/Micron catch-up window vs SK Hynix's lead.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix $26.5B Nasdaq debut (SKHY); 7× oversubscribed but memory stocks in bear market
news_pulse.implication: Second-largest US share sale ever, yet timing collides with sector -20%+ drawdown. Tests whether listing validates AI thesis or marks sentiment peak. Kioxia may follow.

news_pulse.headline: Commerce Sec. Lutnick presses Samsung, SK Hynix to expand US memory production
news_pulse.implication: Political pressure for onshore HBM/DRAM capacity. Could unlock CHIPS Act funding but diverts capex from Korea fabs, complicating 2027-28 supply ramp timeline.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM Q3 forecast: +13-18% QoQ vs Q1 +93-98%, Q2 +58-63%; deceleration confirmed
news_pulse.implication: Sequential pricing growth halving each quarter since Q1 peak. Consumer affordability wall hit; AI/server still tight but spot buyers stepping back. Confirms late-cycle dynamics.

brief.derivatives_signal: <cite index="41-6,41-7,41-8">Samsung/SK leveraged ETFs: $15.4B (23 trillion won) inflows in June, 52.7% of top-10 ETF volume</cite>; <cite index="41-15,41-16">SOL SK Hynix inverse 2X down -43%, leveraged products off -20 to -30%</cite> since May 27 debut. <cite index="41-19,41-20">Samsung + SK Hynix now 55% of KOSPI weight vs 51% pre-ETF launch</cite>—structural rebalancing risk amplifies intraday swings. <cite index="40-2,40-9,40-10">KOSPI circuit-breaker triggered; SK Square -13%, Samsung -9%, SK Hynix -14.6% on July 2</cite>. Retail capitulation signal: single-stock leverage concentration at extremes just as momentum breaks. Watch for dealer gamma flip if spot falls below recent ETF strike clusters.
